## The shark actually goes somewhere now, and Settings stops rearranging your background on the way out

Three fixes and a button, all found by actually staring at the thing long enough.

The aquarium background's rare shark had a bug where it reversed direction the instant it crossed the middle of the screen, which trapped it bouncing left-right around the center forever instead of ever swimming across and leaving. It now commits to one crossing, and while it was open: it's nearly twice as big, prowls with a slow vertical weave instead of sliding on a rail, is actually visible instead of a near-invisible grey wash, has a red eye glint, and startles any fish it swims straight through.

Closing the Settings screen was also quietly cycling your background. The settings gear icon lives in the title bar's top-left corner, which is the same corner CLEAR uses for its tap-to-change-background gesture -- so the exact tap that closed Settings fell straight through into that gesture on the same frame. That gesture was the one tap handler in the whole app missing a debounce guard; it has one now.

### The actually-useful part
- **Fixed**: the aquarium shark oscillating around the center of the screen instead of swimming across and leaving
- **Fixed**: closing Settings via the title-bar gear icon also cycling the CLEAR screen's background
- **Changed**: the shark is bigger, more visible, prowls vertically, and startles fish it passes through
- **Changed**: ALERT's MORE INFO button is now a taller two-line button in the corner instead of a wide one, so it stops crowding the radar and the idle animations
- **Changed**: tapping GOT IT on an alert's explanation now returns straight to the main screen instead of back to the alert you just read about
